resources.string: Reel Counter is not an assistive accessibility tool. It uses this service, only if you turn it on, to: (1) infer when you move to a new short video in the apps you choose to monitor (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok) by reading scroll positions of their video feed; (2) read the address bar of Brave or Chrome to recognise short-video pages and blocked websites; and (3) show the floating counter and the block screen on top of other apps. It does not read messages, passwords, video titles or page contents, does not store what it reads, never sends data off your device, and never taps or scrolls for you. You can turn it off here at any time.
Warnings when you reach the short-video milestones and limits you set.
You have watched %1$d short videos today.
You have watched %1$d short videos. You are approaching your daily limit of %2$d videos.
Your configured short-video limit of %1$d videos has been reached.
You have watched %1$d short videos today; your limit was %2$d.
You have spent %1$d minutes in short-video apps. Your time limit is %2$d minutes.
Your configured time limit of %1$d minutes has been reached.
Some of these counts are estimated.
Your daily short-video limit has been reached.
The whole website is paused. Android does not let Reel Counter pause only part of a site.
You have used all temporary overrides for today.
Temporary overrides are turned off in settings.
Tap again to pause blocking until reset

This is a limit you set yourself. Phone, messages and other essential apps are never blocked. You can change limits in Reel Counter, or turn off its accessibility service in Android Settings, at any time.
